title: vivo T5 5G unveiled: Dimensity 7500 Turbo SoC, 144Hz curved display, and 7,050 mAh battery
description: vivo launched the T5 4G in May, and as promised, the company unveiled the T5 5G today, making it the sixth member of the T5 series. vivo says the T5 5G is "designed for ambitious young hustlers who seek powerful performance, premium design and long-lasting endurance." The vivo T5 5G is powered by the Dimensity 7500 Turbo SoC, paired with up to 12GB of LPDDR4X RAM. It has up to 256GB of UFS 3.1 storage onboard and runs Android 16-based OriginOS 6 out of the box. vivo has promised three Android OS upgrades and five years of security updates for the T5 5G. title: Xiaomi 18 Fold gets its first official look ahead of September 7 launch
description: Xiaomi confirmed last week that its wide-screen foldable will launch in September with the Xring O3 chipset. Now, the company has officially revealed the Xiaomi 18 Fold’s design and confirmed its launch date. The Xiaomi 18 Fold will launch in China on September 7, two days before Apple is expected to unveil its own wide-screen foldable, the iPhone Ultra. Alongside announcing the launch date, Xiaomi also showcased the foldable in a Nishino Red colorway. The phone is seen with a triple rear camera setup and an LED flash housed inside a horizontal, pill-shaped camera module. It also...

title: Oukitel has a rugged industrial tablet, a laptop with a solar panel and home solar batteries
description: In addition to its rugged phones – check them out here – Oukitel unveiled an 11” industrial tablet, a laptop with a solar panel on it and several solar energy solutions for the home and the campsite. Oukitel RT10 series tablets The Oukitel RT10 is an 11” industrial tablet with a fingerprint scanner and a 2D barcode scanner. It has a 1080p 120Hz display and 5W stereo speakers rated for over 130dB. The tablet is powered by the Dimensity 7400X (12GB RAM, 512GB storage, expandable) and a 25,000mAh battery. Oukitel RT10 industrial tablet The industrial version supports...

title: Oukitel unveils a gaming phone with dual fan cooling, a phone with a built-in lighter and more
description: Oukitel arrived at IFA with suitcases full of rugged hardware. There’s a rugged gaming phone, an “ultra-endurance” flagship and even a phone that has a built-in electric lighter. Oukitel WP70 Ultra The Oukitel WP70 Ultra claims to be the slimmest phone with a 16,000mAh battery. The massive silicon-carbon battery supports 66W fast charging. This phone has a 6.78” 120Hz OLED display and is powered by the Dimensity 7200 chipset (this was MediaTek’s first 4nm chipset). The phone launches with Android 16 out of the box. title: Apple’s foldable iPhone Ultra said to feature MagSafe charging
description: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone, rumored to be called the iPhone Ultra, at its September 9 event. Ahead of the launch, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has revealed details about its features and pricing in an interview with Tom’s Guide. In the interview, Gurman also says that the upcoming iPhone Ultra will likely support MagSafe charging, despite leaked renders and dummy units not showing the familiar magnetic ring. Alleged iPhone Ultra (left) dummy doesn't show magnetic ring for MagSafe Gurman believes Apple will be able to include the feature because it managed to...

title: Samsung Galaxy S27 and S27+ bag 3C certification, charging speeds revealed
description: Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 lineup has been the subject of several leaks in recent weeks. Now, the base Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27+ have appeared on China’s 3C certification website, revealing details about their charging capabilities. According to the 3C listing, the Galaxy S27, carrying the model number SM-S9520, will support 25W wired charging. This is the same charging speed offered by its predecessor, the Galaxy S26, as well as the Galaxy S20, which launched several years ago. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S27+ with model number SM-S9560 is listed with support for 45W wired charging....

title: Google announces September Android drop, here are all the new features
description: Today Google has announced its September Android drop, which incorporates five new features coming to Android devices left and right. So let's dive right in. You will "soon" be able to ask Gemini to remember where you put important items and it will save their location in Google's Find Hub so you can easily find them later. This is intended for things you don't put a tracker tag on, like your passport or a spare key. Just tell Gemini where the item is - or maybe add an optional photo. When you need to find it, either ask Gemini for its location or check the remembered items tab in Find...

title: nubia's NaviX Ultra AI phone is coming this month
description: Back in July, nubia first talked about the NaviX Ultra, an "AI-powered smartphone" because nubia didn't want to let a company you've probably never heard of claim that title all by itself. Now the nubia NaviX Ultra has been certified in China by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) - or rather, its built-in AI Large Language Model (LLM) got the green light (as all AI models have to in China, by law). The phone was jointly developed by nubia and ByteDance, the company behind TikTok. It will be available in four colors: blue, black, white, and "Dream". nubia...

title: Poco F9 Pro in for review
description: Looking at the Poco F9 Pro, you'd be forgiven for not wanting an F9 Ultra. Yes, global users are getting a big battery reduction - the Redmi K100 Pro, on which the Poco F9 Pro is based, has a whopper of a battery at 8,580mAh, while the Poco makes do with 6,330mAh. But it's still not bad at all. In the hands, the Poco F9 Pro is a premium-feeling smartphone. It's glass on both sides and brushed metal in the middle. It's also a comfortable slab to handle for long periods, thanks to its reasonably sized 6.59-inch display. A key difference between the Poco F9 Pro and its Ultra...

title: vivo X500 Pro series video capabilities teased ahead of launch
description: vivo recently began teasing its upcoming X500 series and has already confirmed several key camera features of the X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max. The company has now offered a glimpse at the video capabilities of its upcoming Pro models. Last week, vivo confirmed that the X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max will support 4K 240fps slow-motion video recording. The phones will feature a new primary rear camera that uses a custom Phantom 900 sensor co-developed by Sony and vivo’s Blueprint Imaging team. vivo also confirmed that the new sensor offers up to 17EV of dynamic range and 3-axis optical...

title: Google Pics launches to create and edit images in Google Docs, Slides, and Drive
description: Today Google is starting to make Google Pics available. Google Pics is a new service that is not to be confused with Google Photos or Google Images. Google Pics is billed by Google as providing you with "a suite of fine-tuned editing capabilities that let you generate images and make precise edits rather than starting from scratch". Why this couldn't just be a Gemini feature is unclear. It is also using Nano Banana, although Google doesn't say which version. Pics is both a standalone product and integrated into Google Workspace apps, starting with Slides, Docs, and Drive, so it will...

title: Latest leak claims the iPhone 18 Pro lineup will launch in these new colors
description: There have been plenty of rumors surrounding the color options for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro series, and now there’s another one to add to the list. The latest leak reiterates some previous rumors, but notes that the new iPhones will be available in three color options. According to tipster Fixed Focus Digital, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available in Dark Cherry/Burgundy, Sky Blue, and Black colorways. The latest leak contradicts recent rumors that claimed the upcoming iPhones would also be offered in a silver colorway. If this turns out to be accurate,...

title: Xiaomi's Mijia is "entering Europe at scale" at IFA later this week
description: Xiaomi is attending IFA for the first time this year, and the company is aiming big. It will have a press conference on September 3 at 10:30 AM local time in Berlin (that's 9:30 AM in London, 11:30 AM in Eastern Europe, and 2 PM in India). Xiaomi's Mijia - the ecosystem brand that incorporates everything from household appliances to smart home devices and much more, spanning more than 2,000 products in total across over 130 categories - will be the star of the show, it seems. Xiaomi promises that it will bring its smart home experience to "more consumers across Europe". Mijia...

title: The team behind Galaxy Z8's My FanCam explains how the feature works and what inspired it
description: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8, Z Fold8 Ultra and Z Flip8 introduced a feature called My FanCam, which is also featured on the Galaxy S26 FE. The team that developed it shared their inspirations, thoughts and goals for this feature. (From left) Sherry Hong, Sunghwan Kim and Hwangpil Park Sharing fan videos of K-pop performances has become a popular activity among music fans – but until now they had to manually edit the video. My FanCam allows them to create a cut of the video that tracks one person as they move across the stage – all it takes is a single tap. Object tracking isn’t new,...

title: Xiaomi 18 Fold surfaces in benchmark, confirming its chipset and RAM amount
description: Xiaomi has already officially confirmed that it's launching the 18 Fold this month, and that the device will be powered by the self-developed Xring O3 chipset, which seems quite impressive. Now the upcoming foldable smartphone has been spotted in the Geekbench AI online database, as a prototype ran the benchmark. The device is powered by the Xring O3 SoC as expected, paired with 16GB of RAM - at least that's how much the prototype in question had. Xiaomi may offer other options too. The Xiaomi 18 Fold will run Android 17 when it arrives, which is good to see because Google released...

title: Poco X8 is official with an 8,340 mAh battery and the Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 SoC
description: Today's big Poco launch wasn't all about just the F9 Pro and F9 Ultra. Obviously, the flagships got most of the attention, but the brand has also decided to finally make the 'vanilla' Poco X8 official for global markets, ahead of its Indian launch (where the X8 Power is joining it) in a few days. The Poco X8 lands many months after the Pro and Pro Max, which both launched in March. The 'vanilla' model sports a 6.83-inch AMOLED screen with a 1280x2772 resolution, a 120Hz refresh rate, and 3,500-nit peak brightness. It's powered by the Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 SoC. iQOO 16’s unique rear camera module design leaked
description: If recent rumors are accurate, the iQOO 16 could launch sometime this month. While we haven’t heard anything official from iQOO, new details about the phone’s rear camera module have surfaced. title: Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra announced
description: The brand-new Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra share similar designs and specs, though there are enough differences that help the Ultra model stand out. Starting off with the chipset, F9 Ultra brings the top-tier Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip, which has been powering Android flagships for the last twelve months. The F9 Pro gets the recently announced Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series (SM8850-1-AB). According to Qualcomm’s own documents, the V series version of the chip features a slightly watered-down GPU. title: Samsung expands One UI 9 Beta program to more devices, Galaxy S25 series receiving first beta update
description: Samsung announced the Android 17-based One UI 9 Beta program for the Galaxy S26 series in May, and today, the Korean brand expanded the One UI 9 Beta program to more Galaxy devices in India, South Korea, the US, and the UK. The Galaxy devices eligible for the One UI 9 Beta program include the Galaxy Z Fold7, Galaxy Z Flip7, Galaxy S25, Galaxy S25+, Galaxy S25 Ultra, and Galaxy S25 FE. The press release we received from Samsung doesn't mention the Galaxy S25 Edge, so it's unclear whether it will receive One UI 9 beta or get the stable build directly.
